record.source_closeout_reference: User-authorized V3-MC-EPIC-002 deterministic serial mission-state kernel mission.

mission.objective: Implement a deterministic stdlib-only advisory serial mission-state kernel with authored state, append-only events, pure transitions, local CLI, deterministic coverage, and canonical closeout evidence without worker execution or runtime authority.

envelope.reference: The user explicitly approved execution of bounded mission V3-MC-EPIC-002 in the current conversation.

forbidden_scope: no worker dispatch, sub-agent orchestration, Codex SDK execution, or verification-command execution
no concurrent workers, worktree orchestration, background process, daemon, scheduler, or scheduled wake
no runtime authority, proof or lease enforcement, governance routing, telemetry enforcement, or external governance-kernel adapter
no dependency addition, deployment, credential, real-data, required-gate, CI, or profile-promotion work
no Factory V2 removal and no changes to regulated_factory_site
allowed_commands: canonical standalone Factory V3 advisory validators with pinned fixture expectations
python3 scripts/factory_v3_serial_mission_state.py status against the valid templates
authority.dependency_policy: No new dependencies allowed; Python standard library only.
fallback_triggers: scope expands into worker execution, concurrency, runtime authority, required gates, deployment, credentials, or another repository
authored state conflicts with the graph or append-only events
invalid transitions mutate state or append a success event
deterministic fixtures or full repository verification fail at closeout

commands: all canonical V3 advisory validators with pinned fixture expectations
verification.summary: Full repository tests, knowledge lint, context-index refresh, canonical pinned V3 advisory fixtures, valid state-template status, Python compilation, deterministic fixture replay, invalid-transition no-mutation checks, and diff whitespace checks pass. The natural-language pilot completed with its existing non-blocking findings in loop-governance documents; no new finding points to the state-kernel artifact.

observations.command_or_check_ref: full repository verification and pinned advisory replay after documentation closeout
evidence_refs: thread-local command output; not persisted as a separate repository log

notes: The kernel is one standalone stdlib script and reuses the existing graph validator instead of adding a package or dependency.
The CLI has no subprocess, network, worker, daemon, scheduler, or verification execution path.
Persistence documents its cross-file limit, appends events before atomic state replacement, and fails clearly on divergence.
No scope or authority fallback trigger fired; implementation stayed inside the approved advisory state-kernel envelope.

verifier_provenance.unresolved_gap: No distinct verifier actor or fresh session replayed this mission; original and replay observations came from the same actor and session.

boundary_claims.claim: The mission change range adds no worker dispatch, command-execution path, concurrency, daemon, scheduler, runtime authority, required-gate wiring, dependency, or external effect.
boundary_claims.limit: This proves the bounded mission change range and tested local CLI behavior, not global runtime absence outside the repository or future adapters.

boundary_claims.claim: Invalid tested transitions do not mutate the authored source state or append a success event.
boundary_claims.limit: This covers deterministic local fixture cases and does not prove crash-free behavior on every filesystem or untested fault injection point.

boundary_claims.claim: Deterministic fixtures prove live fresh-worker artifact sufficiency or attended serial-epic behavior.
boundary_claims.limit: No fresh worker, separate session, worker adapter, attended epic, or real multi-feature implementation was executed in this mission.

friction_notes: Keeping authored state authoritative while preserving append-only events required an explicit non-atomic cross-file failure model; the design records divergence rather than claiming impossible atomicity or silently truncating events.

The first hold-state invariant treated safe_hold as outside the serial child slot; focused tests showed the current child must remain authored during hold, and validation was corrected before closeout.
The readable lifecycle expected summary exposed a manual off-by-one revision/event count during fixture authoring; the pinned expectation was corrected from observed deterministic output.
false_positive_notes: No mission-record validator false positive was observed for the third natural record.
The valid state/event/graph templates return advisory_pass with no unexpected consistency rejection.
false_negative_notes: The initial in-progress hold-state validation missed that safe_hold must retain the serial current-child slot; focused lifecycle coverage detected and repaired this implementation false negative before final verification.
The lifecycle expected count was initially wrong by one; the deterministic comparison failed clearly instead of allowing the mismatch through.
No known false negative remains in the exercised mission-record validator output, but same-actor testing and the absence of fault-injection or live fresh-worker evidence limit that conclusion.

phase2_design_signals: Three natural optional evidence-integrity records now exist; recurring friction and FP/FN conclusions require a separate comparison of all three.
Authored state, graph contract, append-only evidence, and derived cursors need distinct non-authority roles to avoid a second mission-state source of truth.
Filesystem state/event persistence must disclose and detect cross-file divergence rather than imply atomic transactions.
